arxiv-1402-2073.title: Mining Images in Biomedical Publications: Detection and Analysis of Gel Diagrams
arxiv-1402-2073.creator: Tobias Kuhn, 1 Mate Levente Nagy, 3 ThaiBinh Luong, 2 and Michael Krauthammer 2,3
arxiv-1402-2073.description: Abstract Authors of biomedical publications use gel images to report experimental results such as protein-protein interactions or protein expressions under different conditions. Gel images offer a concise way to communicate such findings, not all of which need to be explicitly discussed in the article text.

arxiv-2201-05128.title: All-optical ultrafast spin rotation for relativistic charged particle beams Preprint: Physical Review Letters
arxiv-2201-05128.creator: Wen-Qing Wei, Feng Wan, Yousef I. Salamin, Jie-Ru Ren, Karen Z. Hatsagortsyan, Christoph H. Keitel, Jian-Xing Li, Yong-Tao Zhao
arxiv-2201-05128.description: Abstract An all-optical method of ultrafast spin rotation is put forward to precisely manipulate the polarization of relativistic charged particle beams of leptons or ions. In particular, laser-driven dense ultrashort beams are manipulated via single-shot interaction with a co-propagating moderate temporally asymmetric (frequency-chirped or subcycle THz) laser pulse.

arxiv-2202-06720.creator: Piero Procacci, Guido Guarnieri
arxiv-2202-06720.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Piero Procacci, Guido Guarnieri. We present our blind predictions for the Statistical Assessment of the Modeling of Proteins and Ligands (SAMPL), 9th challenge, focusing on binding of WP6 (carboxy-pillar[6]arene) with ammonium/diammonium cationic guests. arxiv-2301-09613.title: Anisotropic magnetism and electronic structure of trigonal EuAl 2 Ge 2 single crystals
arxiv-2301-09613.creator: Santanu Pakhira, Asish K. Kundu, Farhan Islam, M. A. Tanatar, Tufan Roy, Thomas Heitmann, T. Yilmaz, E. Vescovo, Masahito Tsujikawa, Masafumi Shirai, R. Prozorov, David Vaknin, D. C. Johnston
arxiv-2301-09613.description: Abstract Understanding the interplay between magnetic and electronic degrees of freedom is of profound recent interest in different Eu-based magnetic topological materials. In this work, we studied the magnetic and electronic properties of the layered Zintl-phase compound EuAl 2 ​ Ge 2 {\rm EuAl_{2}Ge_{2}} crystallizing in the trigonal CaAl 2 ​ Si 2 {\rm CaAl_{2}Si_{2}} -type structure.

arxiv-2304-08718.title: Generalized Implicit Factorization Problem
arxiv-2304-08718.creator: Yansong Feng, Abderrahmane Nitaj ( ✉ ) {}^{(\textrm{{\char 0\relax}})}, Yanbin Pan ( ✉ ) {}^{(\textrm{{\char 0\relax}})}
arxiv-2304-08718.description: Abstract The Implicit Factorization Problem (IFP) was first introduced by May and Ritzenhofen at PKC’09, which concerns the factorization of two RSA moduli N 1 = p 1 ​ q 1 N_{1}=p_{1}q_{1} and N 2 = p 2 ​ q 2 N_{2}=p_{2}q_{2} , where p 1 p_{1} and p 2 p_{2} share a certain consecutive number of least significant bits.

arxiv-2311-02079.title: Analysis of Geometric Phases in Particle Diffusion Systems: Insights from Non-Hermitian Heat Transfer
arxiv-2311-02079.creator: Jinrong Liu, Liujun Xu, Gaole Dai, Gang Wang
arxiv-2311-02079.description: Abstract Geometric phases in particle diffusion systems, an intriguing aspect enlightened from thermal systems, offer a different understanding beyond traditional Brownian motion and Fick’s laws. This concept introduces a phase factor with significant implications for particle behavior, central to which is the non-Hermitian nature of the Hamiltonian in the diffusion system.

arxiv-2407-03892.title: On the Effectiveness of Acoustic BPE in Decoder-Only TTS
arxiv-2407-03892.creator: Bohan Li, Feiyu Shen, Yiwei Guo, Shuai Wang, Xie Chen, Kai Yu
arxiv-2407-03892.description: Abstract Discretizing speech into tokens and generating them by a decoder-only model have been a promising direction for text-to-speech (TTS) and spoken language modeling (SLM). To shorten the sequence length of speech tokens, acoustic byte-pair encoding (BPE) has emerged in SLM that treats speech tokens from self-supervised semantic representations as characters to further compress the token sequence.

arxiv-2408-09839.title: Segment-Anything Models Achieve Zero-shot Robustness in Autonomous Driving
arxiv-2408-09839.creator: Jun Yan, Pengyu Wang, Danni Wang, Weiquan Huang, Daniel Watzenig, Huilin Yin
arxiv-2408-09839.description: Abstract Semantic segmentation is a significant perception task in autonomous driving. It suffers from the risks of adversarial examples. In the past few years, deep learning has gradually transitioned from convolutional neural network (CNN) models with a relatively small number of parameters to foundation models with a huge number of parameters.

arxiv-2412-00150.title: Curriculum Fine-tuning of Vision Foundation Model for Medical Image Classification Under Label Noise
arxiv-2412-00150.creator: Yeonguk Yu, Minhwan Ko, Sungho Shin, Kangmin Kim, Kyoobin Lee, kyoobinlee@gist.ac.kr
arxiv-2412-00150.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yeonguk Yu, Minhwan Ko, Sungho Shin, Kangmin Kim, Kyoobin Lee, kyoobinlee@gist.ac.kr. Deep neural networks have demonstrated remarkable performance in various vision tasks, but their success heavily depends on the quality of the training data. Noisy labels are a critical issue in medical datasets and can significantly degrade model performance. Previous clean sample selection methods have not utilized the well pre-trained features of vision foundation models (VFMs) and assumed that training begins from scratch.

arxiv-2412-15978.title: BabyHGRN : Exploring RNNs for Sample-Efficient Training of Language Models
arxiv-2412-15978.creator: Patrick Haller, Jonas Golde, Alan Akbik
arxiv-2412-15978.description: Abstract This paper explores the potential of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and other subquadratic architectures as competitive alternatives to transformer-based models in low-resource language modeling scenarios. We utilize HGRN2 ( Qin et al. 2024 ) , a recently proposed RNN-based architecture, and comparatively evaluate its effectiveness against transformer-based baselines and other subquadratic architectures (LSTM, xLSTM, Mamba).

arxiv-2510-22434.title: Separation of Unconscious Robots with Obstructed Visibility
arxiv-2510-22434.creator: Prajyot Pyati, Navjot Kaur, Saswata Jana, Adri Bhattacharya, Partha Sarathi Mandal
arxiv-2510-22434.description: Abstract We study a recently introduced unconscious mobile robot model, where each robot is associated with a color , which is visible to other robots but not to itself. The robots are autonomous, anonymous, oblivious and silent, operating in the Euclidean plane under the conventional Look-Compute-Move cycle.

pmc-10693643.title: Whole genomes from Angola and Mozambique inform about the origins and dispersals of major African migrations
pmc-10693643.creator: Sam Tallman, Maria das Dores Sungo, Sílvio Saranga, Sandra Beleza
pmc-10693643.description: As the continent of origin for our species, Africa harbours the highest levels of diversity anywhere on Earth. However, many regions of Africa remain under-sampled genetically. Here we present 350 whole genomes from Angola and Mozambique belonging to ten Bantu ethnolinguistic groups, enabling the construction of a reference variation catalogue including 2.9 million novel SNPs.

pmc-11451578.title: Match workload and international travel associated with (ACL) injuries in professional women's football
pmc-11451578.creator: Steve den Hollander, Alex Culvin, Gino Kerkhoffs, Vincent Gouttebarge
pmc-11451578.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Women's football has grown in popularity, competitiveness and professionalism, increasing the demands placed on players and their injury risk. This study aimed to identify differences in the match workload and international travel between injured and non‐injured professional women's footballers. The study was conducted as an observational, retrospective, case‐control study over two football seasons (2021/2022 and 2022/2023) in four top‐tier European women's football leagues.

pmc-11482484.title: The Role of Lymph-Adipose Crosstalk in Alcohol-Induced Perilymphatic Adipose Tissue Dysfunction
pmc-11482484.creator: Kourtney D Weaver, Liz Simon, Patricia E Molina, Flavia Souza-Smith, Roberto Cannataro, Sandro Michelini, Erika Cione
pmc-11482484.description: Chronic alcohol use leads to metabolic dysfunction in adipose tissue. The underlying mechanisms and the contribution of alcohol-induced adipose tissue dysfunction to systemic metabolic dysregulation are not well understood. In our previous studies, we found that chronic alcohol feeding induces mesenteric lymphatic leakage, perilymphatic adipose tissue (PLAT) inflammation, and local insulin resistance in rats.

pmc-12172753.title: Overlap in the cortical representation of hand and forearm muscles as assessed by navigated TMS
pmc-12172753.creator: Fang Jin, Sjoerd M Bruijn, Andreas Daffertshofer
pmc-12172753.description: The representation of upper limb muscles in the motor cortex is not clear-cut. The motor cortex contains areas that, when stimulated, may activate different muscles simultaneously, hence they seem to overlap. We expected the cortical representations of synergistic muscle pairs to overlap more than those of non-synergistic muscles.

pmc-12369399.title: Prevalence, Associations, and Outcomes of Suprastomal Collapse After Pediatric Tracheostomy
pmc-12369399.creator: Ashley Young, Alexander Szymczak, Taher Valika, Saied Ghadersohi, Inbal Hazkani
pmc-12369399.description: BackgroundSuprastomal collapse is an understudied sequela of pediatric tracheostomy that may hinder decannulation. This study aims to investigate the prevalence and associated risk factors of suprastomal collapse following pediatric tracheostomy.MethodsA retrospective cohort study of children who underwent tracheostomy at a tertiary‐care children's hospital between 1/2012 and 12/2022.ResultsA total of 255 children underwent tracheostomy, with 146 (57.3%) developing suprastomal collapse 10.

pmc-12374920.title: Shear wave elastography for assessing kidneys in pediatric patients with primary nephrotic syndrome
pmc-12374920.creator: Jianhuan Yang, Fangfang Yu, Dexuan Wang, Maosheng Xu, Hongxia Luo
pmc-12374920.description: ObjectivePrimary nephrotic syndrome (PNS) is a prevalent kidney disorder in pediatric patients, characterized by significant proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and edema, which poses serious health risks and economic burdens due to frequent relapses and hospitalizations. This study aims to explore the utility of shear wave elastography (SWE) as a novel, non-invasive biomarker for assessing renal health in this population.

pmc-12801855.title: Alterations in lower limb kinematics and moments in partial foot amputation versus diabetic neuropathy
pmc-12801855.creator: Omar M Elabd, Bassem Galal Eldein El Nahass, Mona Mohamed Ibrahim
pmc-12801855.description: BackgroundGait compensatory mechanisms associated with partial foot amputation (PFA) and peripheral neuropathy (PN) aren’t well understood.PurposeCurrent study aimed to assess deviations in the sagittal plane kinematics and moments of the lower limb joints in PFA due to PN versus PN alone.
